title: Nodal magnon spin current at an antiferromagnet/altermagnet junction
abstract: We investigate the thermally driven magnon spin current across a junction between a $d$-wave altermagnet (AM) and a ferromagnet (FM) or an antiferromagnet (AFM).   The current consists of a component independent of the interface angle and an angularly dependent component with the $d$-wave form.   For a sublattice-symmetric interface, the two junctions behave oppositely under reversal of the altermagnetic domain: in the FM/AM junction the angularly dependent component is odd and cancels on averaging over the domains, whereas in the AFM/AM junction the angularly independent component vanishes by symmetry and the angularly dependent component survives the domain average at a fixed Néel vector of the AFM.   Both follow from a selective tunneling: a pair of spins bonded across the interface transmits magnons when the spins are parallel and not when antiparallel, which makes the AFM/AM junction a magnon valve: the configuration in which the bonded spins are antiparallel blocks the current up to the sublattice admixture of the magnons.   The anisotropic tunneling is detectable as the sign reversal of the current between the interfaces normal to $[310]$ and $[130]$, and the valve reads the Néel vector of the altermagnet relative to that of the antiferromagnet through the magnitude of the current at a fixed interface.
summary: This theoretical work analyzes the thermally driven magnon spin current across junctions between altermagnets and magnetic insulators (FM or AFM). It reveals distinct symmetry behaviors for the two junction types, most notably demonstrating that the AFM/AM junction functions as a magnon valve due to spin-dependent tunneling. The results provide quantitative predictions for controlling spin transport using magnetic order parameters.
main_problem: The paper investigates the thermally driven magnon spin current across junctions involving an altermagnet (AM) coupled to either a ferromagnet (FM) or an antiferromagnet (AFM).
main_result: The AFM/AM junction exhibits a magnon valve effect, where the current is suppressed when the interface spins are antiparallel, and the domain average of the spin current survives even when the uniform component vanishes.
method: The spin current expectation value is calculated using the Keldysh Green’s function method applied to a spin-wave Hamiltonian model.
model_or_system: The system consists of junctions (FM/AM or AFM/AM) modeled by spin-wave Hamiltonians, with the interface coupling treated via a nearest-neighbor interaction Hamiltonian. The analysis focuses on the resulting magnon spin current.
key_observables: Spin current $j_{Sz}(	heta)$, its harmonic components ($c_0, c_2$), and the ratio of currents in different magnetic domains.
important_parameters: Interface angle $	heta$, relative orientation of Néel vectors, and the strength of inter-sublattice exchange couplings ($J_{ex}$).
main_assumptions: The analysis is performed in the sublattice-symmetric interface case, and approximations like the diagonal approximation are used in the calculation of current components.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the dimensionless spin current $g$ vs. angle $	heta$ for both junction types, comparing domain averages and showing the dependence on magnetic domain configurations.
paper_structure: The paper systematically calculates the spin current using Keldysh formalism, contrasting the symmetry properties and domain averaging behavior between FM/AM and AFM/AM junctions, and detailing the mechanism behind the magnon valve effect.
why_interesting: The study of magnon transport and spin currents in magnetic junctions is highly relevant to spintronics and magnonics, providing theoretical insights into novel current control mechanisms like the magnon valve.
